# oncallalert_rotation (Resource)

An on-call rotation: users take turns in shifts.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "oncallalert_rotation" "backend" {
  name         = "Backend weekly"
  time_zone    = "Europe/Berlin"
  start        = "2026-01-05T09:00:00+01:00"
  type         = "weekly"
  shift_length = 1
  user_ids     = [data.oncallalert_user.alice.id, data.oncallalert_user.bob.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name.
- `start` (String) When the first shift starts (RFC3339).
- `time_zone` (String) IANA time zone, e.g. `America/New_York`. Prefer canonical names (`Etc/UTC`, not `UTC`): the server stores aliases under their canonical name, so an imported object with an alias in config shows one no-op update.
- `type` (String) Shift unit: `monthly`, `weekly`, `daily` or `hourly`.

### Optional

- `description` (String)
- `shift_length` (Number) Number of `type` units per shift. Default 1.
- `user_ids` (List of String) User IDs in rotation order.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import oncallalert_rotation.example <id>
```
